adhippāya:
1adhippāya
m., 1. [cf S. abhiprāya], meaning, intention; wish, desire; Abh 766 (ajjhāsayo ~o); Vin III 133,.21 (attakāman ti attano kāmaṃ … attano ~aṃ); D II 160,.14 (aññathā kho Vāseṭṭhā tumhākaṃ ~o aññathā devatānaṃ ~o); S I 124,.31 (uccāvacā kho purisānaṃ ~ā); Th 542 (evaṃ me kattukāmassa ~o samijjhatu); Ja I 83,.14 (thero pi bhagavato ~aṃ viditvā); III 311,5´ (sagge uppajjantī ti ~ena vadati); Nidd I 64,.8 (sakaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ sakaṃ ~aṃ atikkamituṃ); Peṭ 92,.12 (ettha bhagavato ko ~o); Mil 148,.10 (~o ti attano mati); Vism 147,.15 (yena hi ~ena bhagavatā uddeso kato); — ifc see anuvijjanâ-, apaharaṇâ-, ekâ-, kīḷâ-, khuṃsanâ-; — 2. [cf BHS abhiprāya], particular meaning, distinction, difference; M I 64,.24 (ko viseso ko ~o kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be adhippayāso; Ps II 9,.22 : ko adhikapayogo) ≠ S II 24,.11 (Ce, Ee so; Be adhippayāso; Se adhippāyaso; Spk II 278,.1 : ko ~o ti ko adhikapayogo, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se adhippayāso ti) ≠ III 66,.4 (Ce so; Be adhippayāso; Ee adhippāyoso; Se adhippāyaso) ≠ A I 267,.17 (Ce so; Be adhippayāso; Ee adhippāyoso; Se adhippāyaso); —      ° ânusandhi,   f., meaning and application; Pj II 65,.16 (ayaṃ tāv’ ettha padato atthavaṇṇanā ~ito pana evaṃ veditabbā); —       °-ttayika,   mfn., having three meanings or interpretations; Sadd 918,.2 (atthi padaṃ ~aṃ); — see also ekādhippāyika (sv eka), dvādhippāyika (sv dvi), caturādhippāyika (sv catu[r]).

2adhippāya
ind. [absol. of *adhi + pa2 + eti1; cf S. abhipraiti], wishing for; aiming at; Ja VI 36,15* (~a phalaṃ eke … payojayanti kammāni; cf 36,26´ : adhippāyaphalan ti attano adhippāyassa phalaṃ sampassamānā); — see also adhippeta.

bhū:
1bhū
f. [ts] (sg. loc. bhuvi; cf Sadd 238,.10 foll.), 1. being, existence; Dhātup 373 (asa bhuvi); Dhātum 600; Sadd 450,.10 (asa bhuvi); — 2. the earth; the ground; Abh 182; 1052 (mahī … bhuvi); 1059; Ap 539,.31 (sokaṭṭā bhuvi pātitā, Ee so; Be bhūmipātitā; Ce, Se bhūmipātikā); Vism 68,29* (ākaṅkhamāno bhuvi sericāraṃ); Mhv 64:46 (sabbān’ etāni lokamhi yāv’ ajjadivasā bhuvi); Sadd 84,.18 (~ū vuccati paṭhavī); — 3. thriving, welfare; Ps III 165,.3 (~ū ti vaḍḍhi); —      °-dhara, m., a mountain; Abh 605; —       °-nātha, m., a king; Abh 334; —       °-pa, m. [bhū + pa4], a king; Abh 335; Mhv 11:38; 17:54; —       °-pati, m. [bhū + pati2], a king; a ruler; Abh 333; Paṭis-a 704,2*; Mhv 2:12; 5:72; —       °-pāla, m., a king; Abh 333; Mhv 37:170; Sadd 238,.13; —       °-bhuja, m. [bhū + bhuja2], a king; Abh 334; Sadd 238,.13; —       °-ruha, m. [bhū + ruha1], a tree; Sadd 238,.13; —       °-saṇhakaraṇī, f., an instrument for smoothing the earth; Abh 1007 (pāṇi … ~iyaṃ mato); — see also bhūmi-; —     abhū, f., absence of thriving; destruction; Ps III 165,.3 (abhū ti avaḍḍhi, vināso mayhan ti attho); — see also abbhu(ṃ).

bhū2 mfn. [cf S. bhṛt], having; maintaining; — ifc see gotrabhū̆, pāṇabhū̆ (sv pāṇa).

f. [S. bhrū], an eyebrow; Abh 259 (~ū … bhamuko bhamu); 1059; —    subbhu, mfn., with beautiful eyebrows; Ja IV 18,13* (~ū subhā, Be, Ce so; Ee ~u; Se subbhā; 18,17´ : ~ū ti subhamukhā, Be, Ce, Ee so, perhaps wr for subhamukā; Se subbhā ti); 19,29* (sussoṇi ~u suvilākamajjhe, Ce so; Se subbhā; Be subhamu suvilaggamajjhe; Ee subbhuru vilākamajjhe; 20,4´ : ~ū ti sundarabhamuke, Ce so; Be subhamū ti; Ee subbhurū ti; Se subbhā ti) quoted Cp-a 32,11* (eds subbhūru; 32,.17 : subbhūrū ti sundarehi bhamukehi ūrūhi ca samannāgate).
dāya:
1dāya
m. [ts], a gift; a remuneration; Abh 898 (~o dāne); Ja IV 138,.18 (ayaṃ rājā … aṭṭh’ eva kahāpaṇe dāpesi, imassa ~o nahāpitadāyo); V 343,.23 (mahāsattaṃ tassa ~aṃ katvā dadanto āha, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee dāsaṃ) ≠ 363,.23 (ahaṃ etaṃ Sumukhassa ~aṃ katvā vissajjessāmī ti); Mp I 156,.11 (~aṃ dātuṃ yuttaṭṭhāne ~aṃ denti); — ifc see tuṭṭhi-, rāja-.

2dāya
m. [ts], share; inheritance; Abh 898 (~o … vibhattabbadhane ca pitūnaṃ); — ifc see dhamma- (sv dhamma1); —      °’-āda,   mf (n)., (one) who inherits; an heir; Abh 1046 (~o bandhave putte); S IV 72,.17 (app eva nām’ ahaṃ bhagavato bhāsitassa ~o assan ti); A III 72,.4 (yaṃ kammaṃ karissāmi kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā tassa ~o bhavissāmī ti; Mp III 260,.7 foll. : tena dinnaphala-paṭiggāhako bhavissāmī ti attho); 259,.19 (corasādhāraṇā bhogā appiyehi ~ehi sādhāraṇā bhogā); Thī 63 (putto buddhassa ~o Kassapo; Thī-a 73,.29 : tassa dāyabhūtassa navalokuttaradhammassa ādānena ~o); Ja V 468,1* (addhā aññe pi ~e putte lacchāma); VI 151,24* (bhūmipati janapadassa ~o); Ap 22,.31 (tassa dhammesu ~o oraso dhammanimmito Sāriputto ti nāmena; Ap-a 278,.2 : dhammakoṭṭhāsabhāgī); Vism 44,.14 (te hi bhagavato puttā tasmā pitusantakānaṃ paccayānaṃ ~ā hutvā te paccaye paribhuñjanti); Sp 51,.2 (yo hi koci … attano orasaṃ puttaṃ pabbājeti ayaṃ vuccati mahārāja ~o sāsanassā ti); Mp I 308,.15 (dārako ubhinnaṃ pi kulānaṃ ~o hotī ti); Mhv 5:197; — adāyāda, mfn., without heirs; not belonging to an heir; S I 69,.31 (anapaccā adāyādā); Ja III 24,29* (nidhī … adāyādo; 25,11´ : dāyādānaṃ abhāvato adāyādo); —       °’-ādaka,   m., °’-ādikā, f., an heir; an heiress; M II 73,13* (~ā tassa dhanaṃ haranti) = Th 781; Th 1142 (~o hehisi aggavādino); Thī 327 (tuvaṃ dāyādikā kule); — see also dāyajja.

3dāya
dāva1 m. [cf S. dāva], a forest; a park; Abh 536 (araññaṃ kānanaṃ ~o); 898 (~o … vane); Vin II 138,.15 foll. (chabbaggiyā bhikkhū ~aṃ ālimpenti, manussā ujjhāyanti … seyyathā pi davaḍāhakā ti … na bhikkhave ~o ālimpetabbo); M I 205,.23 (mā samaṇa etaṃ ~aṃ pāvisi; Ps II 235,.21 : ~o ti avisesena araññass’ etaṃ nāmaṃ); A IV 74,.2 (gacchaṃ pi daheyya ~aṃ pi daheyya; Mp IV 39,.25 : ~an ti sārakkhaṃ abhayatthāya dinnaṃ araññaṃ); Sn 703 (uccāvacā niccharanti ~e aggisikhūpamā); Ja III 274,11* (taṃ maṃ vadhituṃ āgañchi ~asmiṃ Añjanāvane; 274,17´ : ~asmin ti migānaṃ vasanatthāya dinne uyyāne); —     dāvaggi,   m., a forest fire; Ja III 140,.15 (imasmiṃ araññe ~imhi uṭṭhite kiṃ karothā ti); Vism 470,.19 (doso … attano nissaya-dahanaraso vā ~i viya); Dhp-a I 281,.18 (antarāmagge mahantaṃ ~iṃ uṭṭhitaṃ disvā); —       °’-ālimpana,   n., setting fire to a park; Sp 477,.15 (~-vatthūsu); —       °-pāla,   m., the keeper or guardian of a park; Vin I 350,.32; M III 155,.15 (~o, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se °-pālako); Ps II 236,.15 foll.; —       °-vāsika,   mfn. [dāya + vāsika2], living in a forest (; Ap 198,.2 (~o isi, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se vanavāsiko; Ap-a 465,.10 : vane vasanabhāvena ~o isī ti saṅkhaṃ gato).
gaggarāyamāna:
1gaggarāyamāna
mfn. [part.pr. of *gaggarāyati1, cf S. gadgadyati], making an indistinct noise; Sv 569,.25 (gaggarā [asani] ~ā patati); — see also gaggarāyanta.

2gaggarāyamāna
mfn. [part.pr. of *gaggarāyati2 from *gaggara2 < S. gargara, “whirlpool, eddy”], eddying, whirling; Mil 3,.7 (gaṅgāya ūmivegaṃ ~aṃ disvā; or to gaggarāyamāna1?); — see also gaggalaka.
abbhunnadita:
abbhunnadita
mfn. [pp of (caus. of) *abhi + unnadati], resounding; made to resound; Th 1065 (~ā sikhīhi te selā).

  Order of the Pāli letters
    a ā i ī u ū e o
    ṃ
    k kh g gh ṅ
    c ch j jh ñ
    ṭ ṭh ḍ ḍh ṇ
    t th d dh n
    p ph b bh m
    y r l ḷ ḷh v
    s h
    The anusvāra (the pure nasal ṃ) does not change before y, r, l, v, s, and h; and in that position it comes before all other consonants in the alphabetical order. For example, saṃvara and saṃsaya come before saka.
    Before other consonants, ṃ may change to the class nasal, i.e. that in the same line in the table above. For example, -ṃk- may be written -ṅk-, -ṃc- may be written -ñc-, etc. Thus saṃgha is the same as saṅgha, saṃcaya as sañcaya, etc. Even when the anusvāra is written in that position, its place in the alphabetical order is that of the equivalent class nasal.

adhamma:
1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll. (ahaṃ kho āvuso navo acirappabbajito adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ na t’ ahaṃ sakkomi vitthārena ~aṃ desituṃ api ca te saṅkhittena atthaṃ vakkhāmī ti … ye ~ā hetuppabhavā tesaṃ hetuṃ tathāgato āha tesaṃ ca yo nirodho evaṃvādī mahāsamaṇo; Sp 975,.19 : ye ~ā hetuppabhavā ti hetuppabhavā nāma pañcakkhandhā); III 1,.18 (iti pi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho … so imaṃ lokaṃ … sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti so ~aṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhe kalyāṇaṃ pariyosāna-kalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ savyañjanaṃ …); D I 62,.24 foll. (tathāgato loke uppajjati … so ~aṃ deseti … taṃ ~aṃ suṇāti gahapati … taṃ ~aṃ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṃ paṭilabhati … so aparena samayena … agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati); II 55,.14 (etassa Ānanda ~assa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evaṃ ayaṃ pajā tantākulakajātā … apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ saṃsāraṃ nātivattati); M I 37,.20 (svākkhāto bhagavatā ~o sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opanayiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī ti; cf Vism 213,.16 foll. : svākkhāto ti imasmiṃ hi pade pariyattidhammo pi saṅgahaṃ gacchati itaresu lokuttaradhammo va); (in Be kathina), n. [BHS id.; cf AMg kaḍhina; Sp-ṭ (Be) III 335,.1 foll. : kathinan ti pañcānisaṃse anto-karaṇasamatthatāya thiran ti attho ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ], 1. a framework (covered with a mat) to which the cloth for making robes was attached while being sewn; Vin II 116,.10 foll. (anujānāmi bhikkhave ~aṃ kaṭhinarajjuṃ tattha tattha obandhitvā cīvaraṃ sibbetun ti. visame ~aṃ pattharanti ~aṃ paribhijjati; Sp 1206,.7 : ~an ti nisseṇiṃ pi tattha attharitabbakaṭasārakakilañjānaṃ aññataraṃ pi); 117,.26 foll. (bhikkhū cīvaraṃ sibbetvā tatth’ eva ~aṃ ujjhitvā pakkamanti, undurehi pi upacikāhi pi khajjati … anujānāmi bhikkhave ~aṃ saṃharitun ti. ~aṃ paribhijjati, anujānāmi bhikkhave goghaṃsikāya ~aṃ saṃharitun ti ~aṃ viveṭhiyati …); — esp. kaṭhinaṃ attharati (i) spreads or covers the kaṭhina, ie makes a robe using the kaṭhina; — (ii) participates, at the end of the rains-residence, in a communal robe-making, during which certain rules and practices are suspended (perhaps in order to facilitate the robe-making); this involves a) a saṅghakamma allotting the material (and the use of the kaṭhina ) to a bhikkhu according to need and seniority; b) the preparation of the robe, by all the participating bhikkhu s, from washing the cloth to adding the kappabindu qv; c) the approval of the robe by one or more bhikkhu s. Only those can take part and share the privileges who have spent the earlier rain-retreat within that sīmā and have participated in the pavāraṇā ceremony. A minimum of five bhikkhu s is required, but unqualified ones may make up the number without sharing the privileges. The donor gives cloth, sewing materials and food to the participating bhikkhu s. The whole process must be completed in one day. cf Vin I 254,.25 foll. and Sp 1107,.10 foll.; Vin I 254,.8 (anujānāmi bhikkhave vassaṃ vutthānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ~aṃ attharituṃ); 254,.19 (saṅgho imaṃ kaṭhinadussaṃ itthan-nāmassa bhikkhuno deti ~aṃ attharituṃ); M III 126,.10 (nābhijānāmi ~e cīvaraṃ sibbitā; Ps IV 193,.19 : ~e cīvaran ti kaṭhinacīvaraṃ, kaṭhinacīvaraṃ pi hi vassāvāsika-gatikam eva); Sp 1108,.10 (kaṭhinatthārasāṭakaṃ labhitvā suṭṭhu dhovitvā sūci-ādīni cīvarakammupakaraṇāni sajjetvā bahūhi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ tadaheva sibbitvā niṭṭhitasūcikammaṃ rajitvā kappabinduṃ datvā ~aṃ attharitabbaṃ); — (iii) displays the finished robe; Vin V 176,.22 foll. (tena kaṭhinatthārakena bhikkhunā tadaheva dhovitvā vimajjitvā vicāretvā chinditvā sibbetvā rajitvā kappaṃ katvā ~aṃ attharitabbaṃ. sace saṅghāṭiyā ~aṃ attharitukāmo hoti porāṇikā saṅghāṭi paccuddharitabbā navā saṅghāṭi adhiṭṭhātabbā imāya saṅghāṭiyā ~aṃ attharāmī ti vācā bhinditabbā … evaṃ assa vacanīyo atthataṃ bhante saṅghassa ~aṃ dhammiko kaṭhinatthāro anumodathā ti); — kaṭhinaṃ atthataṃ, as well as referring to the literal covering of the kaṭhina and the proper carrying-out of the communal robe-making, also describes a state existing in an āvāsa where qualified bhikkhu s have a claim on material given to the saṅgha (and on the use of the kaṭhina ) and enjoy the five concessions or privileges; Vin I 254,.25 foll. ind. [S. tiras], across, beyond; apart, secretly; obliquely; Abh 1159 (~o tu tiriyaṃ); Ap-a 449,.15 (pakārena ~o hutvā patiṭṭhahatī ti pabbato); —      °-’ kkha,   mfn. [tiro + akkha4; cf S. parokṣa], out of sight; not present; secret; Vin III 185,.8 (ye sammukhā te passanti ye ~ā te suṇanti); — ~-vāca, mfn., speaking in someone’s absence;? telling secrets;? with secret, hidden words;? Ja V 78,5* (~-vāco asataṃ paviṭṭho; 79,3´ : ~-vāco ti attano yaṃ vācaṃ bhāsitukāmo tassā ~-katattā paṭicchannavāco, Be so; Ce tirokatattā; Ee tassa ~-kattā; Se tassā tirokatattā appaṭicchannavāco); — tirokkhā, adv., out of sight; in someone’s absence; Ja III 89,6* (sammukkhā vā ~ā vā yo sante na paribhāsati, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee parokkhā); —       °-karaṇa,   n., concealing; Bv-a 102,.7 (kavāṭakuḍḍapabbatā āvaraṇaṃ ~aṃ kātuṃ asakkontā); 196,.27 (āvaraṇan ti paṭicchādanaṃ ~aṃ); — see also tirokaroti; —       °-karaṇī,   f. (and °-karaṇī̆ya, n.?), a curtain, a screen; Abh 298 (~ī); Vin I 276,.9 (~iṃ parikkhipitvā thambhe ubbandhitvā, Ce, Se so; Be, Ee ~iyaṃ); II 152,.15 (anujānāmi bhikkhave ~in ti, ~iṃ ukkhipitvā olokenti); III 16,.24 (~iyaṃ parikkhipitvā, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se ~īyaṃ; Sp 210,.11 foll. : ~iyan ti karaṇatthe bhummaṃ, sāṇipākārena parikkhipitvā ti attho, atha vā tirokaronti etenā ti ~iyaṃ, taṃ parikkhipitvā samantato katvā ti attho, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se ~īyan ti … ~īyaṃ …); Ud-a 312,.11 (cīvaraṃ ~īyaṃ katvā); Th-a I 61,.19 (~iṃ parikkhipitvā adaṃsu); —       °-kucchigata,   mfn., within the womb; D II 13,.16 (bodhisattaṃ ca bodhisattamātā ~aṃ passati sabbaṅgapaccaṅgiṃ ahīnindriyaṃ; Sv 436,.7 : ~an ti antokucchigataṃ); Ap 507,.11 (mātu me dohaḷo āsi ~assa me); —       °-kuḍḍa (Be always    °-kuṭṭa),    m.n., 1. (m.) the other side of a wall; the area beyond a wall; Pj I 206,.12 (~ā ti kuḍḍānaṃ parabhāgā vuccanti); — 2. (n.) the“ Tirokuḍḍa sutta ” ( Khp 7 = Pv 5 ); Pj I 201,23* (yena yattha yadā yasmā ~aṃ pakāsitaṃ); 216,.20 (~ena vā puññavirahitānaṃ vipattiṃ dassetvā); — ~aṃ (and ~ā), through a wall; to the other side of a wall; D I 78,.3 (~aṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gacchati seyyathā pi ākāse; Vism 394,.14 : ettha ~an ti parakuḍḍaṃ kuḍḍassa parabhāgan ti vuttaṃ hoti); A IV 55,.11 (mātugāmassa saddaṃ suṇāti ~aṃ vā tiropākāraṃ vā hasantiyā vā bhaṇantiya vā) quoted Vism 52,.24 (Ce, Ee, Se ~ā; Be °-kuṭṭā); Ap 374,.3 (~aṃ tiroselaṃ … passāmi cakkhunā ahaṃ) ≠ 571,.13 (Ce, Se so; Be °-kuṭṭaṃ; Ee °-kuḍḍhaṃ); — ~e, ~amhi, over the wall; on the other side of the wall; Vin IV 265,.11 (kaṭāhe vaccaṃ katvā ~e chaḍḍentī; 266,.7 : kuḍḍassa parato); Ja IV 470,25* (~amhi gāyitvā; 472,8´ : ~amhī ti sayanagabbhakuḍḍassa bahi); — ~esu, on the other side of the walls; outside the walls; Khp 7:1 (~esu tiṭṭhanti) = Pv 5:1 (Pv-a 24,.12 : kuḍḍānaṃ parabhāgesu); —        °-kkāra,   m., disrespect, abuse; Abh 172 (avamāno ~o); —       °-gaticcha,   mfn., whose desire has disappeared; Saddh 130 (~ā dhammesu tiracchānā tato matā); —       °-gāma,   m. [tiro + gāma2], another (distant) village; Vin III 135,.27 (Sp 553,.6 : ~o bahigāmo, añño gāmo ti adhippāyo); —       °-gāmaka,   m., one who lives outside the village, in another (distant) village; Vin III 135,.23; —        °-(c)chada,   mfn., on the other side of the fence; Ja VI 60,24* (addakkhiṃ phaliṃ ambaṃ ~aṃ, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee phalaṃ; 61,9´ : ~an ti °-pākāraṃ uyyānassa anto ṭhitaṃ bahipākāraṃ nissāya jātaṃ ambarukkhaṃ addasaṃ, Be, Ee, Se so; Ce antoṭhito va); —        °-janapada,   m., another (distant) district or country; D I 116,.1 (samaṇaṃ … Gotamaṃ °-raṭṭhā ~ā sampucchituṃ āgacchanti; Sv 286,.24 : ~ā ti parajanapadato); Ja VI 423,26* (tibbo saddo ~e suto, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ~aṃ; 423,29´ foll. : pararaṭṭhesu para-janapadesu); Sp 873,.24 (°-raṭṭhesu ~esu ca); Ps I 100,.21 (dūrato pī ti °-raṭṭhato pi ~ato pi); —       °-dussantena,   ind. turati pr. 3 sg. [cf S. tvarate and √tur], is in a hurry, makes haste; runs; Th 291 (yo dandhakāle ~ati) ≠ Ja III 141,2*; Sadd 426,.3 (tara sambhame: … ~ati); — part.pr. (a) neg. atara(t), mfn., Vin II 231,15* (in uddāna: omuñci chattaṃ khandhe ca ataraṃ ca); (b) taranta2, mfn., Th-a II 123,.29 (dandhayitabbe ~anto); — neg. ataranta, mfn., Sv 252,.19 (ataramāno ti ataranto, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se aturito); (c) taramāna2, mfn., M III 230,.20 (ataramāno va bhāseyya no ~amāno ti); Ja IV 433,8* (uṭṭhehi samma ~amāno); VI 423,6* (na sirī ~amānassa; 423,9´ : ataramānassa sirī hoti ~amānena kataṃ kammaṃ na sobhati); Bv 1:49 (~amānā upāgamuṃ; Bv-a 47,.31 : ~amānā ti turitā); Vism 105,.13; — taramānarūpa, mfn., in great haste, absolutely hurrying; S I 50,.27; Sn 417 (~amānarūpo niyyāsi); Ja V 166,25* (gacch’ eva kho tvaṃ ~amānarūpo); VI 302,4* (hand’ ehi dānī ~amānarūpo dīgho hi addhā ayaṃ puratthā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr hand’ esa hīdāni); — neg. ataramāna, mfn., Vin II 208,.3 (ataramānena ārāmo pavisitabbo); D II 178,.13 (ataramāno deva yāhi yathā taṃ mayaṃ cirataraṃ passeyyāmā ti); — ataramāno in Ce, Ee at Th-a III 200,.29 is prob. wr for acirāyamāno (Be, Se so); — aor. 2 sg. turittho, Ja VI 229,11* (saṃsārasuddhi sabbesaṃ mā turittho anāgate, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se turito); — absol. neg. ataritvā2, aturitvā, Ja I 136,22´ (ataritvā avegāyitvā, Be, Ce so; Se aturitvā; Ee aturitvā avegā hitvā); —     pp     turita,    tarita,   mfn. and n. [S. tvarita], 1. (mfn.) in a hurry; hastening; Abh 379 (~o); Vin IV 161,.13 (so brāhmaṇo saritvā ~o ādhāvitvā); Sn 1014 (~ā pabbatam āruhuṃ); Vv 80:8 (so māsakhettaṃ ~o avāsariṃ; Vv-a 311,.8 : ~o ti ~o sambhamanto) quoted Sadd 426,.4 foll. (tarito avāsarin ti pāḷī nidassanaṃ, tattha tarito ti ~o sambhanto); Spk I 24,.5 (rattindivānaṃ taritabhāvo; cf Spk I 23,.24 foll. : rattiyo … puggalaṃ … tarayanti sīghaṃ sīghaṃ gamayanti); Pv-a 181,.7 (~o hutvā taramānarūpo hutvā); Mhv 5:75; — turitaṃ, adv., in haste; quickly; Abh 40 (~aṃ); Thī 482 (āruhi ~aṃ); Sp 280,.16 (agginā daḍḍho viya ca ~aṃ vuṭṭhāsi); — 2. (n.) haste; Sp 170,24* (bhaye kodhe pasaṃsāyaṃ ~e … kare āmeṇḍitaṃ budho); — turitābhi-nipāti(n), mfn., rushing in haste; Ja II 7,26*; — turitaturita, mfn., in very great haste; running quickly; Ja V 178,.28; Mil 147,.17 (te gāmikā āṇāpakassa vacanena ~-turitā sannipatitvā); Vism 259,.4 (~-turitā vilumpanti); — ~-turitaṃ, ~-turitena, adv., Ja I 89,.29 (rājā … ~-turitaṃ nikkhamitvā vegena gantvā); IV 490,.28 (kalyāṇaṃ hi ~-turiten’ eva kātabbaṃ, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se turiten’ eva); Mp V 58,.15 (bhagavā taṃ ~-turitaṃ āgacchantaṃ disvā); Dhp-a III 4,.11 (abhittharethā ti ~-turitaṃ sīghasīghaṃ kareyyā ti attho); — neg. aturita, mfn., Vin V 163,.31 (aturitena bhavitabbaṃ); Sv 252,.19 (ataramāno ti aturito, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee ataranto) = Mp V 29,.10 (eds so); Ap-a 476,.8 (aturito saṇikaṃ assamaṃ gañchin ti); — atiturita, mfn., hurrying too much; atituritaṃ , adv., in too great haste; Ja II 7,.23 (asamekkhitvā atituritaṃ karontānaṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee asamekkhita-atituritaṃ); VI 342,17´ (atituritā nikkhamittha, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se atituritaṃ nikkhamitvā); Mhv 5:62 (so rājātiturito tato); — see also tuṇṇaṃ; — fpp., (something) requiring haste; (where) there should be haste; (a) taraṇīya, (mf)n., Th 291 (yo dandhakāle tarati taranīye ca dandhaye) ≠ Ja III 141,2*; (b) taritabba2, (mf)n., M II 241,.6 (na codanāya taritabbaṃ, puggalo upaparikkhitabbo, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se coditabbaṃ; Ps IV 30,.16 : na codanatthāya gantabbaṃ, Ce, Ee so; Be vegāyitabbaṃ; Se codāyitabbaṃ); Th-a II 123,.29 (dandhayitabbe taranto taritabbe vā dandhayanto); —      caus. pr. 3. sg.     tāreti,        ~ayati2,  tareti,  tarayati,   hurries; urges forward; S I 3,4* (accenti kālā tarayanti rattiyo; Spk I 23,.25 : rattiyo atikkamamānā puggalaṃ maraṇūpagamanāya tarayanti sīghaṃ sīghaṃ gamayanti) = Ja IV 487,22* (cf 488,4´ : tarayantī ti atucchā hutvā āyusaṅkhāraṃ khepayamānā gacchanti); Th 293 (yo dandhakāle dandheti taraṇīye ca ~aye) ≠ Ja III 141,4* (~ayi; 141,10´ : ~ayī ti turitakātabbāni kammāni turito va karoti); Ja VI 554,30* (brāhmaṇo ca tareti no, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be dhāreti); 555,16* (tadāyaṃ asito dhāto na bāḷhaṃ tarayeyya no, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be dhārayeyya); 555,17* (bāḷhaṃ ~eti brāhmaṇo, Ce, Ee so; Se tarati; Be dhāreti); — absol. tārayitvā2, Bv 5:31 (tāraṇīye ~ayitvā bodhanīye ca bodhayī; Bv-a 160,.5 : tāraṇīye ti tārayitabbe); — fpp (a) tāraṇīya, mfn., Bv 5:31; (b) tārayitabba2, mfn., Bv-a 160,.5.
